name: stem-changing verbs
title: Spanish Stem-Changing Verbs Practice: E→IE, O→UE, E→I Quiz
description: Practice Spanish stem-changing verbs: e to ie, o to ue, e to i, the boot pattern, jugar and -ir preterite changes, with 10 sentences checked as you tap.
answer: Stem-changing verbs change the last vowel of the stem in the present when it is stressed: querer → quiero, poder → puedo, pedir → pido. The change happens in yo, tú, él and ellos but not in nosotros, so the forms make a boot shape in a chart. Jugar changes u to ue. Only -ir verbs keep a change in the preterite: pidió, durmieron.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127b.csv

rules.example: querer: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, quieren
poder: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, pueden
pedir: pido, pides, pide, pedimos, piden

quiz.after: ir a la playa este fin de semana.

quiz.before: En el restaurante, mi papá siempre

quiz.after: a las doce en la cafetería.

quiz.why: Jugar changes u to ue: juegan.
Nosotros keeps the infinitive stem: preferimos.
-ir verbs change o to u in the preterite él form: durmió.
-ir verbs change e to i in the preterite ellos form: pidieron.

mistakes: Changing the stem in nosotros: «queremos», «podemos» and «pedimos» keep the infinitive vowel.
Forgetting the change: «yo podo» should be «yo puedo», «ella quere» should be «ella quiere».
Changing -ar and -er verbs in the preterite: «pensó» and «volvió» are regular; only -ir verbs change there.
Using o → ue for jugar's spelling: it is juego, with u → ue, not «joego».
Changing the wrong vowel in long verbs: preferir becomes prefiero (the second e), not «priefero».

heritage: Heritage speakers usually conjugate these verbs by ear. In some families you will hear «pidió» and «pedió», or «sirvieron» and «servieron»; written Spanish uses the stem-changed forms pidió and sirvieron. Also note that nosotros keeps the original vowel: podemos, never «puedemos».
teacher: Draw a boot on the board around the yo, tú, él and ellos forms and leave nosotros outside. Teams race to fill the boot for verbs called out by the teacher, then say one true sentence with each.

faq.question: What is a boot verb?
faq.answer: A stem-changing verb, named for the shape its changed forms make in a conjugation chart: yo, tú, él and ellos change and form a boot, while nosotros (and vosotros) stay outside it.

faq.question: Do stem changes happen in every tense?
faq.answer: No. In the present, they happen when the stem is stressed. In the preterite, only -ir verbs change, and only in the él and ellos forms (pidió, durmieron). -ar and -er verbs have a regular preterite.

faq.question: How do I know if a verb changes its stem?
faq.answer: You cannot tell from the infinitive: pensar changes (pienso) but pasar does not (paso). Dictionaries usually show it as pensar (ie) or dormir (ue, u). Learn the most frequent ones as a group.
